cards.note: As the ending of a word it is toneless zi: 杯子 [bēizi] = cup.
A woman 女 with a child 子.
Counts people and most things: 一个人 = one person. Toneless ge after a number in speech.
Means son or child in words such as 儿子 [érzi] = son; in Beijing speech it is also the -r ending.
Mostly toneless de, marking possession: 我的 = my. Read dì in 目的 [mùdì] = goal, dí in 的确 [díquè] = indeed. Written white 白 plus ladle 勺.
A number before 十 multiplies it, one after it adds: 二十 = 2 × 10, 十二 = 10 + 2.
女人 is the word for a woman in speech: 她是女人. 女 is rarely a word on its own; it marks female in other words (女儿, 女生) and on signs, such as a toilet door.
杯子 is the object: 一个杯子 = a cup. 杯 alone counts what is in it, 一杯水 = a glass of water, and starts words such as 茶杯 [chábēi] = teacup.
Person 人 and mouth 口: the mouths to feed. 中国人口 = the population of China.
A day or date to remember (那天是好日子), or the days of one's life: 过日子 [guò rìzi] = to get by, to live.
